subject: African savanna elephant
sourceTitle: File:016a Desert-adapted elephant dust bathing in Damaraland Photo by Giles Laurent.jpg
creator: Giles Laurent
sourceDescription: Desert-adapted elephant dust bathing in Damaraland, Namibia. Desert-adapted elephants often dust-bathe by spraying sand or dust over their bodies with their trunks. This behavior helps protect their skin from intense sun and heat, acts as a natural insect repellent, and creates a protective layer that reduces moisture loss in the harsh desert environment. Desert-adapted elephants are the same species than African bush elephants (Loxodonta africana) but have behavior and physical adaptations for life in extreme desert environments. They are generally slimmer and slightly smaller than typical bush elephants and weighing toward the lower end of the species’ range due to limited food availability. Although African bush elephants can live 60–70 years in the wild, desert-living populations often have shorter average lifespans (40-50 years) because of the harsh conditions they live in.

subject: Alpine ibex
sourceTitle: File:046 Male Alpine ibexes fighting during mating season in Grammont Photo by Giles Laurent.jpg
creator: Giles Laurent
sourceDescription: Male Alpine ibexes fighting during mating season in Grammont, Switzerland. Male Alpine ibexes engage in ritualized fights during the mating season to establish dominance and determine access to females. By clashing their horns, they assess strength and endurance while minimizing serious injury, with dominant males gaining priority in mating opportunities.
